prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1395; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed collision in a parking lot involving the insured's vehicle and a second vehicle. The claimant reports a shoulder injury from the impact and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Recorded a recorded statement from the claimant, who described the sequence of events in the same way as the initial report. The claimant confirmed they were the driver of the vehicle at the time.

Entry 3: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver is listed as a named insured, and that coverage was in force when the loss occurred. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 4: Obtained photographs of the vehicle damage. The pattern and location of the damage match the impact described by the claimant and the other driver.

Entry 5: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the collision happened as the claimant described it. Witness statements gathered so far align with both accounts.

Entry 6: Police report reviewed. The responding officer's notes confirm the claimant was seated in the vehicle when the collision occurred.

Entry 7: Requested prior claim history and vehicle records. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on record, and no previous claims were located for this vehicle.

Entry 8: Claimant provided treatment records for the shoulder injury. The reported injury fits the type and force of a collision of this kind.

Entry 9: Medical file shows a course of treatment typical for a soft tissue shoulder injury, with visits tapering as the claimant's range of motion and pain improved.

Entry 10: Claimant disclosed a minor strain to the same shoulder many years ago, which healed fully with no lasting limitation. Records from that episode were requested for completeness.

Entry 11: Claimant's account has remained consistent across every contact so far, including the initial report, the recorded statement, and follow-up calls.

Entry 12: File review complete. The accident, vehicle damage, injury, and treatment all appear consistent with one another, and the claim is ready for settlement evaluation.
